stem: A paediatric intern is preparing a non-imminent suspected risk of significant harm report for chronic neglect; which information is most important to include?

options.text: Only the child’s name and the clinician’s overall impression
Child details, family background, and incident details including date, type of risk, and person causing harm
A full completed investigation proving the allegation before submission
Only whether the Child Wellbeing Unit has already accepted the case
The forensic medical findings from the Child Protection Unit before any report is made

explanation: Child details, family background, and incident details are the key information to include in a suspected risk of significant harm report. A report should document the date, type of risk, and the person causing harm when known, and it does not depend on a completed investigation or forensic assessment first.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: How to report

rationale: Document concrete identifying, family, and incident information when making a significant-harm report. Non-imminent significant-harm concerns may be submitted via e-report forms. Reporting does not depend on first completing a full investigation or forensic assessment.

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because the report requires more than the child’s name and a general clinical impression.
optionExplanations.B: Correct because the report should include child details, family background, and incident details such as the date, type of risk, and person causing harm.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because a full completed investigation is not required before reporting; reasonable suspicion is enough to act.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because prior acceptance by the Child Wellbeing Unit is not a prerequisite for making the report.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because forensic findings from the Child Protection Unit are not required before submitting a suspected risk of significant harm report.

sourceRefs: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
